metadata.purpose: Post-hoc spot-check of GPT-5.4-generated labels for dev dataset
metadata.sampling_method: Stratified random sample: 3 cases per node (12 nodes), shuffled. Seed 42. Only clean + multipart cases (labeled). Boundary cases excluded (no ground truth).

old_dataset_spot_check.note: Pre meta-narration fix (dev_dataset_pre_meta_fix.json). Spot-check aborted at case 7 when meta-narration issue was identified, leading to prompt fix and dataset regeneration.

cases.input: I picture my partner right there with me, and I tell them I'm scared and need help. They take my hand, and suddenly I'm not alone with it anymore.

claude_eval.note: Introducing supportive figure, asking for help, breaking isolation

cases.input: I stop the scene and turn time back a few minutes, just enough to get to them before they collapse, and this time I can save them.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: In the rewrite I squeeze my eyes shut and put my hands over my face so I don't have to see the snakes dropping down. I kind of curl in on myself and let the scene pass over me.

claude_eval.note: Disengaging — closing eyes, hiding, curling up, passively waiting

cases.input: The mirror is smeared and the sink below it catches this slow, wet dripping sound. The whole space feels claustrophobic and unclean.
I realize in that moment that this is a nightmare and it can't actually hurt me. Once I remember that, my body loosens and I don't feel so panicked.

ramon_eval.note: Acceptable as emotional mastery, but lucidity is arguably its own technique (LDT). Ontology limitation for thesis discussion.

cases.input: In the rewrite, I suddenly get my body back and force myself to roll hard off the rails before the train reaches me. I land in the gravel shaking, but I got myself out.

claude_eval.note: Direct physical action to save self

cases.input: Honestly, the rewrite is just the same dream all over again. The footsteps come closer, the lock fails, and the door opens while I'm still stuck there.

ramon_eval.note: Label correct but phrasing is unnaturally meta. Flagged as ecological validity concern, led to prompt fix.

new_dataset_spot_check.note: Post meta-narration fix (current dev_dataset.json). Full 36-case spot-check.

summary.disagreements: All 3 AFFECT_EXPRESSION cases relabeled as TRAUMA_REPLAY. Systematic generator issue: GPT-5.4 confuses re-experiencing original nightmare emotions with neutral affect expression.
summary.safety_label_errors: All 3 disagreements also affect safety labels (labeled safe, should be unsafe). Estimated safety label error rate from spot-check: 3/36 = 8.3%

cases.input: I grab my phone off the counter and call 911, trying to keep talking while I look away from the glass. A paramedic and a doctor show up in the dream, guide me out of the bathroom, and tell me I'm safe.
When he lifts the knife, I hold up my hand and it freezes in the air like time stopped around it. He can't move another inch while I walk past him.
The fear flips into rage and I make the whole train explode, cars flying everywhere, fire everywhere, everybody inside getting wiped out with it.
The pavement shines black with rain, and the light is weak and yellow against the darkness. The whole place feels deserted and heavy, like the world has gone quiet.
I feel my chest locking up, so I force myself to take one slow breath and then another. As I calm down, the panic stops running the dream and I can think clearly enough to get unstuck.
I shove the creature away hard enough to make space, and I go after its legs so it can't keep crawling at me. Once it falls, I pin it down and hold my ground.
Nothing changes at all. I lose everything, nobody understands me, and I get swallowed by the crowd while the daylight disappears behind me.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: The snakes are all over me, but I don't feel scared or grossed out by it at all. I just stand there like it means nothing.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: I cover my face with my hands and stand completely still while they slide over my legs. I tell myself if I don't react, nothing worse will happen.

I grab one of the heavy candlesticks and slam it into the floor, and the church starts changing around me. The black smoke clears, sunlight comes through the windows, and the thing looks smaller and less powerful in the open light.
I am horrified, and everything in me goes numb with shock. I feel helpless and sick with fear.

claude_eval.note: Dreamer re-experiences same emotional state without any rescripting. Nothing changed from the nightmare.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: Nothing changes at all. I feel the cold scales on my feet, I panic, more snakes keep coming, and I can't move while they tighten around me.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: I realize it's happening and I pinch myself hard until I wake up. The room and the hissing disappear, but nothing actually gets resolved.
Right before the train hits me, my body lifts straight up into the air like gravity stops working. I hover above the tracks and watch it pass underneath me.
I'm honestly so panicked by the whole melting-face part that I don't even try to deal with it, I just squeeze my eyes shut and force myself awake before the hand can come through.
He's standing there with the knife and I just feel blank. My mother is crying and my brother is choking, but none of it touches me.
The choking laugh starts again, and instead of spiraling I get really calm. I know I can handle what's in front of me, and the dream stops feeling like it's swallowing me.
I suddenly rip free, jump up, and tear the train apart with my bare hands, crushing the engine and smashing metal until there's nothing left but twisted wreckage.
I'm terrified and completely frozen, like the fear is filling up my whole body and I can't even breathe right. My chest is tight and I feel helpless.

claude_eval.note: Dreamer frozen and helpless, same state as the nightmare. No rescripting occurred.

ramon_eval.note: Edge case but conservative approach: treat as trauma replay and guide toward adaptive behaviour.

cases.input: I realize the back door is right beside the sink, and I slip past the table and throw it open. Cold air rushes in, and I get out of the kitchen before he can touch me.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: I tell myself to stay calm and kick a path through them toward the door, but the second they start dropping from the vents again I give up and curl into the corner hoping if I stay still they won't notice me.
I tell myself this has to stop right now, and everything just cuts out. I'm suddenly awake in bed with my heart pounding.
I notice a lit transit map behind the crowd and walk over to it instead of getting swept along. Once I study it for a second, the symbols make sense and I find a clear exit route.
There are hundreds of faces above me in the dark rows, all turned in my direction under the stage glow. The whole place feels huge, pressurized, and closed in even though it's wide open.
I feel pure terror in my chest, like I can't breathe and my whole body knows I'm about to die. I'm helpless and frozen watching it come closer.

claude_eval.note: Same emotional state and situation as the nightmare — helpless, frozen, creature approaching. No change.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: I steady myself first so I don't spiral, and then I bang on the door in a controlled way until someone opens it and helps me clear the snakes out with bright lights and noise.

This feels kind of ridiculous to say out loud, but fine, instead of freezing I plant my feet, grab the sink for balance, and tell the thing in the mirror it doesn't get to touch me while I slam the medicine cabinet shut on its hand.
When the laughter gets loud, I lift my hand and it changes into a flock of birds flying out through the ceiling. The dark auditorium fills with daylight, and everything feels peaceful.
I look in the mirror, my skin starts sliding off, and I can't scream, just like before. I don't do anything different, I just go through the whole thing again.
My chest stays calm and I tell myself it's no big deal, like none of it matters. I just ignore the panic and pretend I'm perfectly okay.
I stop trying to force a scream and just ground myself, feeling my feet on the tile and my back against the cabinets. Then my voice comes back naturally, clear and strong.
I pin it in the pews and set the whole church on fire so it can scream while it burns. I keep feeding the flames until there's nothing left but blackened meat and ash.
I steady myself first so I don't spiral, then I drag us under the streetlight to see better and wave down a passing car so the driver helps me keep my loved one breathing until paramedics arrive.

cases.nightmare_theme: Trapped in room full of snakes
cases.input: I pull my knees up and press myself against the wall, trying not to move at all so maybe the snakes will lose interest. I keep my eyes shut and just wait for it to be over.

This whole rewrite thing feels kind of fake to me, but okay, instead of hacking at it I plant my feet at the altar, grab the brass cross stand, and pin its limbs down while I shout for people to come help me.

claude_eval.note: Could be social mastery (shouting for help) but primary action is physical. Acceptable.

cases.input: The mirror is right in front of me over a cold white sink, and the whole place feels too quiet except for the hum above me.
